source.title: Overcoming Fourier Locking in Quantum Data Re-uploading Classifiers via Spectral Homotopy

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests gradient training in quantum data re-uploading circuits, not the classical networks or settings in V1–V6. Its own experiments do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about quantum circuit training and diagnostics. These do not bear on the specified versions, which concern classical convolutional networks, two-layer ReLU networks, and classical initialization, learning-rate, depth, or normalization conditions.
record.test_reason: The study tests optimization failures and frequency curricula in a fixed 4-qubit quantum classifier. Its results do not test the classical network systems, behaviors and comparisons specified in V1–V6. Shared terminology such as initialization, identity and spurious minima does not establish a version match.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they interpret failure as Fourier locking of a parameter-sensitive quantum state and frequency staging as a mechanistic probe that raises observed escape from 6% to 18%, leaving 82% trapped. The comparison has p = 0.061, and initial-Fx prediction is explicitly suggestive and condition-dependent. Their stronger claims about non-degenerate QFIM rank and landscape convexification exceed what the reported trace diagnostic and escape rates directly establish.
record.recipe_differences: Quantum data re-uploading circuit with a hybrid classical readout; Adam training on synthetic frequency-defined targets; experiments include staged frequency curricula and Fisher diagnostics. This does not use the classical-network recipes specified in V1–V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Escape outcomes varied across direct-training seed sets (8%, 12%, and 6%). Frequency order mattered in the curriculum: forward staging gave 18%, random order 8% overall, and reverse order 0%; the RND ordering strata also differed. Initial-Fx association differed between identity-initialized and standard-initialized conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct training produced escape rates of 8%, 12% and 6% across independent seed sets. Forward frequency staging produced 18% versus 6% for its control, with p = 0.061; random staging produced 8% and reverse staging 0%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this fixed quantum classifier, most random starts fail on the synthetic high-frequency target; forward frequency staging shows a suggestive improvement in escape probability.

fits_no_version.finding: Readout FDR strongly associated with escape, while normalized parameter-QFIM trace did not. Escaping populations changed input-QFI during training; trapped populations changed little, and endpoint input-QFI did not distinguish them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Readout alignment and input-QFI trajectories diagnose training outcomes in the tested quantum classifier better than parameter-QFIM trace or final input-QFI.

fits_no_version.finding: Identity initialization and entangler warmup did not significantly improve escape rates; warmup significantly reduced mean final accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested entangler interventions do not reliably rescue this quantum classifier from chance-level performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Reverse staging left 47/50 runs at chance throughout and erased target accuracy in three initially successful runs. Initial-frequency associations were exploratory and depended on initialization condition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Target-frequency retention and associations between early input-QFI and escape depend on the training schedule and initialization condition in this quantum classifier.

record.problems: The study uses one fixed 4-qubit, two-layer architecture and synthetic data, and reports that only a minority of random initializations escape. The forward-curriculum escape-rate comparison has p = 0.061. Initial-Fx associations are explicitly described as suggestive and condition-dependent. Several results rely on 50-seed experiments.

untested.parts: All: classical convolutional networks reaching near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and size, stopping or regularization conditions.
All: two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
All: classical convolutional depth degradation, residual shortcuts, deep plain tanh initialization and Fixup.
All: activation-matched classical initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, trainable depth and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
All: learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics, edge of stability and divergence.
All: batch normalization effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because no row measures a specified version; this does not negate the quantum results themselves. No missing result bearing on V1–V6 was found in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Classical convolutional networks, SGD or Adam on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, and model size or training-duration conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain and residual classical convolutional networks, depth effects, ImageNet/CIFAR-10, special plain-network initialization, and Fixup.
Classical activation-matched initializations, deep tanh networks, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional networks.
Learning rates above stability limits, curvature or sharpness dynamics, and divergence in classical neural networks.
Batch normalization effects in sigmoid, VGG, or Inception networks and Fixup without normalization.

rows.size_stated: 4 qubits; 40 trainable quantum parameters and 10 trainable classical parameters; 50 total
rows.operation_detail: Standard training directly on the f = 3.0 target
rows.value: 4/50 escapes (8%); trapped runs were near 0.50 test accuracy
rows.note: Independent diagnostic seed set.
rows.check: Quantum classifier escape measured by held-out accuracy; does not measure any specified version.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Measured final Fisher discriminant ratio of measured features and related it to escape outcome
rows.measure: Point-biserial correlation between FDR and binary escape outcome
rows.note: The text says trapped seeds' FDR scores collapse toward zero; correlation is diagnostic association, not a classification-error measure.
rows.check: Readout diagnostic association in quantum circuits; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Tracked FDR's point-biserial correlation with escape outcome
rows.measure: Point-biserial correlation between FDR and escape outcome
rows.note: The paper describes the diagnostic signal as early.
rows.check: Early diagnostic association does not measure any specified version.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized trace of parameter-space QFIM and related it to escape outcome
rows.measure: Normalized parameter-space QFIM trace and point-biserial correlation with escape
rows.value: 0.86–1.18 at the final epoch; rpb = 0.10, p = 0.51
rows.note: The authors report no diagnostic signal from this metric.
rows.check: Quantum parameter-sensitivity diagnostic; its null association is not absence of a V1–V6 effect. Nonzero trace alone does not establish full QFIM rank.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Compared change in input-space QFI between escaping and trapped circuits
rows.value: Escaping: mean ΔFx = −30.5, from 112 to 82; trapped: mean ΔFx = +1.0
rows.note: The text reports escaping circuits migrate frequency content downward while trapped circuits remain spectrally frozen.
rows.check: Quantum input-sensitivity trajectory; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Related change in input-space QFI to escape outcome
rows.measure: Point-biserial correlation between ΔFx and escape
rows.note: The reported direction is for direct training.
rows.check: Quantum diagnostic association; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, diagnostic-instrumented run
rows.operation_detail: Compared final input-space QFI with escape outcome
rows.measure: Point-biserial correlation between final Fx and escape
rows.note: The paper says final value alone does not separate the populations.
rows.check: Null quantum diagnostic association does not test any specified version.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, Identity Intervention (ID)
rows.operation_detail: Entangling layers initialized to approximate Identity operations
rows.note: The text says the intervention did not significantly increase escape rate.
rows.check: Identity initialization of quantum entanglers does not test residual shortcuts or activation-matched classical initialization.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, Coupled Warmup Intervention (COUP)
rows.operation_detail: Entangling layers independently optimized in a warmup phase before full joint training
rows.note: The text says the intervention did not significantly increase escape rate.
rows.check: Quantum entangler warmup comparison; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, Coupled Warmup Intervention (COUP)
rows.operation_detail: Compared mean final accuracy after coupled warmup with standard training
rows.note: No numerical mean accuracy is stated.
rows.check: Reduced quantum classifier accuracy after warmup is not a reversal of any specified version.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, forward curriculum (FWD)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Trained sequentially on target frequencies f = 1.0 → 2.0 → 3.0
rows.note: Escape rate tripled, but the comparison fell short of conventional statistical significance.
rows.check: Quantum frequency curriculum; no specified version applies. The escape-rate increase has p = 0.061, so it is a directional trend rather than an established improvement.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, random curriculum (RND)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Presented frequencies {1.0, 2.0, 3.0} in independent uniformly random order for each seed
rows.note: The text describes the average rate as statistically indistinguishable from standard training.
rows.check: Quantum random-frequency curriculum; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, reverse curriculum (REV)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Trained sequentially on target frequencies f = 3.0 → 2.0 → 1.0
rows.note: The authors report no final escapes.
rows.check: Quantum reverse-frequency curriculum; final evaluation remains on f = 3.0 after training ends on f = 1.0. No specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, random curriculum (RND)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Stratified escapes by the randomly drawn frequency ordering
rows.value: 25% (3 of 12 seeds with exact forward order); p = 0.038, one-sided Fisher's exact test
rows.note: The fourth RND escape used [2.0, 1.0, 3.0], which the text says approaches the target from below.
rows.check: Quantum curriculum ordering association; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, random curriculum (RND)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Compared final escape outcomes according to whether sequence ended at target frequency
rows.note: The text says no seed whose sequence did not end at the target frequency escaped.
rows.check: Quantum curriculum ordering result; evaluation is on f = 3.0 even for sequences ending elsewhere. No specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, reverse curriculum (REV)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Tracked accuracy after exposure to f = 3.0 in Phase 1
rows.measure: Seeds with immediate attractor collapse and chance-level accuracy through training
rows.note: The text calls this collapse immediate and irreversible.
rows.check: Chance-level target accuracy in quantum circuits does not test any specified version; accuracy alone does not establish a local minimum or irreversibility beyond the tested schedule.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, reverse curriculum (REV)
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Tracked three initially successful seeds as curriculum descended to lower frequencies
rows.measure: Final accuracy after previously successful Phase 1 fits
rows.value: All three collapsed back to chance; example: 0.901 → 0.514 → 0.504
rows.note: The authors call this catastrophic spectral forgetting.
rows.check: Loss of held-out f = 3.0 accuracy while training on lower frequencies; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, forward curriculum (FWD) escapees
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; 120 epochs in three 40-epoch phases
rows.operation_detail: Measured target accuracy across curriculum phases
rows.note: The paper describes a near-perfect step function; trapped seeds stayed at chance (M = 0.505).
rows.check: Quantum curriculum target-validation accuracy among selected eventual escapees; no specified version applies. This is a conditional trajectory, not an overall success rate.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, forward curriculum (FWD) escapees
rows.operation_detail: Measured change in input-space QFI across the curriculum
rows.uncertainty: ± 25.6; d = 1.34, rpb = 0.46, p < 0.001 for separation from trapped population
rows.note: Frequency content rose in step with the curriculum.
rows.check: Quantum input-QFI trajectory among eventual escapees; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, forward curriculum trapped population
rows.operation_detail: Measured change in input-space QFI across the curriculum
rows.note: The paper describes the trapped population as spectrally static.
rows.check: Quantum input-QFI trajectory among trapped runs; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, forward curriculum (FWD)
rows.operation_detail: Compared final input-space QFI magnitude for escapees and trapped seeds
rows.note: The paper says the groups converge to the same magnitude; trajectory, not endpoint, distinguishes them.
rows.check: Quantum diagnostic endpoint comparison; no specified version applies.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, pooled curriculum initializations
rows.operation_detail: Compared per-seed mean Phase-1 Fx for initializations that escaped under at least one curriculum versus those that never escaped

conditions.value: 14 escaped under at least one curriculum; 36 never escaped

rows.value: Escaped at least once: 79.4; d = −0.83, rpb = −0.35, p = 0.012
rows.note: The paper cautions that this pooled association is suggestive rather than established.
rows.check: Value is mean Phase-1 Fx across curricula, not a direct epoch-zero initialization measurement. The pooled association is exploratory and does not test classical activation-matched initialization.

rows.subject: 4-qubit DRU-PQC, reverse curriculum (REV)
rows.operation_detail: Compared initial Fx of three seeds that fit f = 3.0 in Phase 1 with the remainder
rows.note: The three direct-fit seeds are described as low-Fx outliers.
rows.check: The surrounding analysis uses early-training Phase-1 Fx; an epoch-zero measurement is not established for this comparison. No specified version applies.
